chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad, said:

I wrote to him: May I be made your ransom. Our companions have narrated from Abu Ja'far and Abu 'Abd Allah عليهما السلام that they both said: When the sun passes the zenith, the time of the two prayers has entered, except that before it there is a supererogatory prayer; if you wish, you may lengthen it, and if you wish, you may shorten it. And some of your adherents have narrated from them عليهما السلام that the time of Zuhr is at two feet from the zenith, and the time of 'Asr is at four feet from the zenith; so if you pray before that, it does not suffice you. And some of them say: that is permissible, but the merit is in waiting for the two feet and the four feet. I wished, may I be made your ransom, to know the place of merit in the time.
So he عليه السلام wrote: The two feet and the four feet are both correct, and this does not contradict that.

key_terms.أَرْبَعَةُ أَقْدَامٍ: four feet; a measure based on shadow length used for prayer timing
key_terms.زَالَتِ: passed the zenith; the sun's decline from midday marking the start of prayer time
key_terms.سُبْحَةً: a supererogatory prayer performed before the obligatory prayer
key_terms.وَقْتُ: the appointed time for performing the prayer
key_terms.ٱلزَّوَالِ: solar noon decline, the point after which Zuhr time begins
key_terms.ٱلصَّلَاتَيْنِ: the two prayers, meaning Zuhr and 'Asr
key_terms.ٱلْفَضْلَ: the superior merit or virtue in choosing a particular timing
key_terms.ٱلْقَدَمَانِ: two feet; a measure based on shadow length used for prayer timing

ai.seo_question: How does al-Istibsar explain the apparent difference between praying at zawal and waiting two or four feet for Zuhr and 'Asr?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the beginning of the times for Zuhr and 'Asr prayers and addresses reports that appear to differ regarding immediate permissibility after zenith versus the merit of waiting until the shadow reaches two or four feet. The Imam عليه السلام affirms that both reports are correct and that there is no contradiction between them.
